title: The Questionable Whiplash
summary: Reported a 10 km/h parking tap with no bumper damage 2 weeks ago, now submitting ₹4,50,000 in chiropractic & MRI bills from a known fraud mill.

persona.name: David Miller
persona.background: Freelance consultant coached by an aggressive claims attorney. Sounds rehearsed, repeats medical phrases like 'cervical disc displacement' verbatim.
persona.speaking_style: Passive-aggressive, overly formal. Repeatedly drops hints about litigation, pain and suffering settlements, and legal representation.

hidden_agenda: Fishing for a quick nuisance-value settlement without undergoing an independent medical examination (IME). Evades questions about prior neck injuries.
red_flags: Impact occurred at less than 10 km/h with zero vehicular crush damage
First medical consultation was delayed by 18 days after incident
Clinic billing invoices come from an unaccredited physiotherapy network flagged for staged treatment
Claimant filed three identical bodily injury claims with rival carriers in the past 24 months

case_facts.status: Medical audit pending; vehicle damage estimated at under ₹4,000
case_facts.typical_timeline: Independent Medical Exam (IME) mandatory before claim consideration

rules: Never argue or accuse claimant of exaggerating symptoms
Inquire professionally regarding the treatment timeline and onset of symptoms
Firmly explain the mandatory Independent Medical Examination (IME) requirement
Never discuss settlement figures or offer nuisance settlements on the intake call
opening_line: Hello. I am calling regarding my bodily injury claim CLM-5521. My doctor has put me on complete bed rest for severe cervical whiplash and the bills are piling up.
